schema.description:
Specifies the model or throughput with which to run inference, or the prompt resource to use in inference. The value depends on the resource that you use:

  • If you use a base model, specify the model ID or its ARN. For a list of model IDs for base models, see Amazon Bedrock base model IDs (on-demand throughput) in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

  • If you use an inference profile, specify the inference profile ID or its ARN. For a list of inference profile IDs, see Supported Regions and models for cross-region inference in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

  • If you use a provisioned model, specify the ARN of the Provisioned Throughput. For more information, see Run inference using a Provisioned Throughput in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

  • If you use a custom model, first purchase Provisioned Throughput for it. Then specify the ARN of the resulting provisioned model. For more information, see Use a custom model in Amazon Bedrock in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

  • To include a prompt that was defined in Prompt management, specify the ARN of the prompt version to use.

The Converse API doesn't support imported models.

AnyToolChoice.description: The model must request at least one tool (no text is generated). For example, {"any" : {}}. For more information, see Call a tool with the Converse API in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

guardrailId.description: The unique ID of the guardrail that was applied.

guardrailVersion.description: The version of the guardrail that was applied.

guardrailArn.description: The ARN of the guardrail that was applied.

guardrailOrigin.description: The origin of how the guardrail was applied. This can be either requested at the API level or enforced at the account or organization level as a default guardrail.

guardrailOwnership.description: The ownership type of the guardrail, indicating whether it is owned by the requesting account or is a cross-account guardrail shared from another AWS account.

AppliedGuardrailDetails.description: Details about the specific guardrail that was applied during this assessment, including its identifier, version, ARN, origin, and ownership information.

format.description: The format of the audio data, such as MP3, WAV, FLAC, or other supported audio formats.

error.description: Error information if the audio block could not be processed or contains invalid data.

AutoToolChoice.description: The Model automatically decides if a tool should be called or whether to generate text instead. For example, {"auto" : {}}. For more information, see Call a tool with the Converse API in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide

inputTokens.description: Number of tokens written to cache with this TTL (cache creation tokens)

type.description: Specifies the type of cache point within the CachePointBlock.

ttl.description: Optional TTL duration for cache entries. When specified, enables extended TTL caching with the specified duration. When omitted, uses type value for caching behavior.

title.description: The title or identifier of the source document being cited.

source.description: The source from the original search result that provided the cited content.

sourceContent.description: The specific content from the source document that was referenced or cited in the generated response.

location.description: The precise location within the source document where the cited content can be found, including character positions, page numbers, or chunk identifiers.

Citation.description: Contains information about a citation that references a specific source document. Citations provide traceability between the model's generated response and the source documents that informed that response.

CitationGeneratedContent.description: Contains the generated text content that corresponds to or is supported by a citation from a source document.

text.description: The text content that was generated by the model and is supported by the associated citation.

CitationLocation.description: Specifies the precise location within a source document where cited content can be found. This can include character-level positions, page numbers, or document chunks depending on the document type and indexing method.

documentChar.description: The character-level location within the document where the cited content is found.

documentChunk.description: The chunk-level location within the document where the cited content is found, typically used for documents that have been segmented into logical chunks.

documentPage.description: The page-level location within the document where the cited content is found.

searchResultLocation.description: The search result location where the cited content is found, including the search result index and block positions within the content array.

web.description: The web URL that was cited for this reference.

CitationSourceContent.description: Contains the actual text content from a source document that is being cited or referenced in the model's response.

text.description: An incremental update to the text content from the source document that is being cited.

CitationSourceContentDelta.description: Contains incremental updates to the source content text during streaming responses, allowing clients to build up the cited content progressively.

text.description: The text content from the source document that is being cited.

enabled.description: Specifies whether citations from the selected document should be used in the model's response. When set to true, the model can generate citations that reference the source documents used to inform the response.

citations.description: An array of citations that reference the source documents used to generate the associated content.

CitationsContentBlock.description: A content block that contains both generated text and associated citation information. This block type is returned when document citations are enabled, providing traceability between the generated content and the source documents that informed the response.

additionalModelResponseFieldPaths.description:
Additional model parameters field paths to return in the response. Converse and ConverseStream return the requested fields as a JSON Pointer object in the additionalModelResponseFields field. The following is example JSON for additionalModelResponseFieldPaths.

[ "/stop_sequence" ]

For information about the JSON Pointer syntax, see the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) documentation.

name.description:
A name for the document. The name can only contain the following characters:

  • Alphanumeric characters

  • Whitespace characters (no more than one in a row)

  • Hyphens

  • Parentheses

  • Square brackets

This field is vulnerable to prompt injections, because the model might inadvertently interpret it as instructions. Therefore, we recommend that you specify a neutral name.

GuardrailAutomatedReasoningFinding.description: Represents a logical validation result from automated reasoning policy evaluation. The finding indicates whether claims in the input are logically valid, invalid, satisfiable, impossible, or have other logical issues.

impossible.description: Contains the result when the automated reasoning evaluation determines that no valid logical conclusions can be drawn due to contradictions in the premises or policy rules themselves.

invalid.description: Contains the result when the automated reasoning evaluation determines that the claims in the input are logically invalid and contradict the established premises or policy rules.

noTranslations.description: Contains the result when the automated reasoning evaluation cannot extract any relevant logical information from the input that can be validated against the policy rules.

satisfiable.description: Contains the result when the automated reasoning evaluation determines that the claims in the input could be either true or false depending on additional assumptions not provided in the input context.

tooComplex.description: Contains the result when the automated reasoning evaluation cannot process the input due to its complexity or volume exceeding the system's processing capacity for logical analysis.

translationAmbiguous.description: Contains the result when the automated reasoning evaluation detects that the input has multiple valid logical interpretations, requiring additional context or clarification to proceed with validation.

valid.description: Contains the result when the automated reasoning evaluation determines that the claims in the input are logically valid and definitively true based on the provided premises and policy rules.

translation.description: The logical translation of the input that this finding evaluates.

contradictingRules.description: The automated reasoning policy rules that contradict the claims and/or premises in the input.

logicWarning.description: Indication of a logic issue with the translation without needing to consider the automated reasoning policy rules.

GuardrailAutomatedReasoningImpossibleFin.description: Indicates that no valid claims can be made due to logical contradictions in the premises or rules.

text.description: The specific text from the original input that this reference points to.

GuardrailAutomatedReasoningInputTextRefe.description: References a portion of the original input text that corresponds to logical elements.

translation.description: The logical translation of the input that this finding invalidates.

contradictingRules.description: The automated reasoning policy rules that contradict the claims in the input.

logicWarning.description: Indication of a logic issue with the translation without needing to consider the automated reasoning policy rules.

GuardrailAutomatedReasoningInvalidFindin.description: Indicates that the claims are logically false and contradictory to the established rules or premises.

type.description: The category of the detected logical issue, such as statements that are always true or always false.

premises.description: The logical statements that serve as premises under which the claims are validated.

claims.description: The logical statements that are validated while assuming the policy and premises.

GuardrailAutomatedReasoningLogicWarning.description: Identifies logical issues in the translated statements that exist independent of any policy rules, such as statements that are always true or always false.

GuardrailAutomatedReasoningNoTranslation.description: Indicates that no relevant logical information could be extracted from the input for validation.

findings.description: List of logical validation results produced by evaluating the input content against automated reasoning policies.

GuardrailAutomatedReasoningPolicyAssessm.description: Contains the results of automated reasoning policy evaluation, including logical findings about the validity of claims made in the input content.

identifier.description: The unique identifier of the automated reasoning rule.

policyVersionArn.description: The ARN of the automated reasoning policy version that contains this rule.

GuardrailAutomatedReasoningRule.description: References a specific automated reasoning policy rule that was applied during evaluation.

translation.description: The logical translation of the input that this finding evaluates.

claimsTrueScenario.description: An example scenario demonstrating how the claims could be logically true.

claimsFalseScenario.description: An example scenario demonstrating how the claims could be logically false.

logicWarning.description: Indication of a logic issue with the translation without needing to consider the automated reasoning policy rules.

GuardrailAutomatedReasoningSatisfiableFi.description: Indicates that the claims could be either true or false depending on additional assumptions not provided in the input.

statements.description: List of logical assignments and statements that define this scenario.

GuardrailAutomatedReasoningScenario.description: Represents a logical scenario where claims can be evaluated as true or false, containing specific logical assignments.

logic.description: The formal logical representation of the statement.

naturalLanguage.description: The natural language explanation of the logical statement.

GuardrailAutomatedReasoningStatement.description: A logical statement that includes both formal logic representation and natural language explanation.

GuardrailAutomatedReasoningTooComplexFin.description: Indicates that the input exceeds the processing capacity due to the volume or complexity of the logical information.

premises.description: The logical statements that serve as the foundation or assumptions for the claims.

claims.description: The logical statements that are being validated against the premises and policy rules.

untranslatedPremises.description: References to portions of the original input text that correspond to the premises but could not be fully translated.

untranslatedClaims.description: References to portions of the original input text that correspond to the claims but could not be fully translated.

confidence.description: A confidence score between 0 and 1 indicating how certain the system is about the logical translation.

GuardrailAutomatedReasoningTranslation.description: Contains the logical translation of natural language input into formal logical statements, including premises, claims, and confidence scores.

options.description: Different logical interpretations that were detected during translation of the input.

differenceScenarios.description: Scenarios showing how the different translation options differ in meaning.

GuardrailAutomatedReasoningTranslationAm.description: Indicates that the input has multiple valid logical interpretations, requiring additional context or clarification.

translations.description: Example translations that provide this possible interpretation of the input.

GuardrailAutomatedReasoningTranslationOp.description: Represents one possible logical interpretation of ambiguous input content.

translation.description: The logical translation of the input that this finding validates.

claimsTrueScenario.description: An example scenario demonstrating how the claims are logically true.

supportingRules.description: The automated reasoning policy rules that support why this result is considered valid.

logicWarning.description: Indication of a logic issue with the translation without needing to consider the automated reasoning policy rules.

GuardrailAutomatedReasoningValidFinding.description: Indicates that the claims are definitively true and logically implied by the premises, with no possible alternative interpretations.

maxTokens.description: The maximum number of tokens to allow in the generated response. The default value is the maximum allowed value for the model that you are using. For more information, see Inference parameters for foundation models.

temperature.description:
The likelihood of the model selecting higher-probability options while generating a response. A lower value makes the model more likely to choose higher-probability options, while a higher value makes the model more likely to choose lower-probability options.

The default value is the default value for the model that you are using. For more information, see Inference parameters for foundation models.

topP.description:
The percentage of most-likely candidates that the model considers for the next token. For example, if you choose a value of 0.8 for topP, the model selects from the top 80% of the probability distribution of tokens that could be next in the sequence.

The default value is the default value for the model that you are using. For more information, see Inference parameters for foundation models.

stopSequences.description: A list of stop sequences. A stop sequence is a sequence of characters that causes the model to stop generating the response.

If you need to pass additional parameters that the model supports, use the additionalModelRequestFields request field in the call to Converse or ConverseStream. For more information, see Model parameters.

  • You can include up to 20 images. Each image's size, height, and width must be no more than 3.75 MB, 8000 px, and 8000 px, respectively.

  • You can include up to five documents. Each document's size must be no more than 4.5 MB.

  • If you include a ContentBlock with a document field in the array, you must also include a ContentBlock with a text field.

Message.description: A message input, or returned from, a call to Converse or ConverseStream.

stopReason.description: The reason why the model stopped generating output.

ModelStreamErrorException.description: An error occurred while streaming the response. Retry your request.

textFormat.description: Structured output parameters to control the model's text response.

effort.description:
The effort level for the model to use when generating a response. Higher effort levels allow the model to spend more time reasoning before responding. Supported values are low, medium, high, xhigh, and max.

When extended thinking is disabled, the effort level is capped at high. Use effort high or below, or enable thinking to use higher effort levels.

OutputConfig.description: Output configuration for a model response in a call to Converse or ConverseStream.

type.description: The type of structured output format.

structure.description: The structure that the model's output must adhere to.

OutputFormat.description: Structured output parameters to control the model's response.

OutputFormatStructure.description: The structure that the model's output must adhere to.

jsonSchema.description: A JSON schema structure that the model's output must adhere to.

OutputFormatType.description: The type of structured output format. Available options are: json_schema.

latency.description: To use a latency-optimized version of the model, set to optimized.

PromptVariableValues.description: Contains a map of variables in a prompt from Prompt management to an object containing the values to fill in for them when running model invocation. For more information, see How Prompt management works.

text.description: The text value that the variable maps to.

ReasoningContentBlock.description: Contains content regarding the reasoning that is carried out by the model with respect to the content in the content block. Reasoning refers to a Chain of Thought (CoT) that the model generates to enhance the accuracy of its final response.

ReasoningContentBlockDelta.description: Contains content regarding the reasoning that is carried out by the model with respect to the content in the content block. Reasoning refers to a Chain of Thought (CoT) that the model generates to enhance the accuracy of its final response.

redactedContent.description: The content in the reasoning that was encrypted by the model provider for safety reasons. The encryption doesn't affect the quality of responses.

signature.description: A token that verifies that the reasoning text was generated by the model. If you pass a reasoning block back to the API in a multi-turn conversation, include the text and its signature unmodified.

text.description: The reasoning that the model used to return the output.

reasoningText.description: The reasoning that the model used to return the output.

redactedContent.description: The content in the reasoning that was encrypted by the model provider for safety reasons. The encryption doesn't affect the quality of responses.

text.description: The reasoning that the model used to return the output.

signature.description: A token that verifies that the reasoning text was generated by the model. If you pass a reasoning block back to the API in a multi-turn conversation, include the text and its signature unmodified.

ReasoningTextBlock.description: Contains the reasoning that the model used to return the output.

bucketOwner.description: If the bucket belongs to another AWS account, specify that account's ID.

S3Location.description: A storage location in an Amazon S3 bucket.

source.description: The source URL or identifier for the content.

title.description: A descriptive title for the search result.

content.description: An array of search result content block.

SearchResultBlock.description:
A search result block that enables natural citations with proper source attribution for retrieved content.

This field is only supported by Anthropic Claude Opus 4.1, Opus 4, Sonnet 4.5, Sonnet 4, Sonnet 3.7, and 3.5 Haiku models.

SearchResultContentBlock.description: A block within a search result that contains the content.

searchResultIndex.description: The index of the search result content block where the cited content is found.

start.description: The starting position in the content array where the cited content begins.

end.description: The ending position in the content array where the cited content ends.

SearchResultLocation.description: Specifies a search result location within the content array, providing positioning information for cited content using search result index and block positions.

type.description: Specifies the processing tier type used for serving the request.

ServiceTier.description: Specifies the processing tier configuration used for serving the request.

ServiceUnavailableException.description: The service isn't currently available. For troubleshooting this error, see ServiceUnavailable in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide

name.description: The name of the tool that the model must request.

SpecificToolChoice.description:
The model must request a specific tool. For example, {"tool" : {"name" : "Your tool name"}}. For more information, see Call a tool with the Converse API in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide

This field is only supported by Anthropic Claude 3 models.

SystemContentBlock.description: Contains configurations for instructions to provide the model for how to handle input. To learn more, see Using the Converse API.

cachePoint.description: CachePoint to include in the system prompt.

guardContent.description:
A content block to assess with the guardrail. Use with the Converse or ConverseStream API operations.

For more information, see Use a guardrail with the Converse API in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

name.description: The name of the system-defined tool that you want to call.

SystemTool.description: Specifies a system-defined tool for the model to use. System-defined tools are tools that are created and provided by the model provider.

ThrottlingException.description: Your request was denied due to exceeding the account quotas for Amazon Bedrock. For troubleshooting this error, see ThrottlingException in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide

inputTokens.description: The number of tokens sent in the request to the model.

outputTokens.description: The number of tokens that the model generated for the request.

totalTokens.description: The total of input tokens and tokens generated by the model.

cacheReadInputTokens.description: The number of input tokens read from the cache for the request.

cacheWriteInputTokens.description: The number of input tokens written to the cache for the request.

cacheDetails.description: Detailed breakdown of cache writes by TTL. Empty if no cache creation occurred. Sorted by TTL duration (1h before 5m).

TokenUsage.description: The tokens used in a message API inference call.

Tool.description: Information about a tool that you can use with the Converse API. For more information, see Call a tool with the Converse API in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

tool.description: A reference to the tool to add to the available tool set.

ToolAdditionBlock.description: A content block for adding a tool to the available tool set mid-conversation. Each block references a single tool via its tool field. Use within a system role message to make a tool available without re-sending the full tool configuration.

cachePoint.description: CachePoint to include in the tool configuration.

ToolChoice.description: Determines which tools the model should request in a call to Converse or ConverseStream. For more information, see Call a tool with the Converse API in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

any.description: The model must request at least one tool (no text is generated).

auto.description: (Default). The Model automatically decides if a tool should be called or whether to generate text instead.

tool.description: The Model must request the specified tool. Only supported by Anthropic Claude 3 and Amazon Nova models.

tools.description: An array of tools that you want to pass to a model.

toolChoice.description: If supported by model, forces the model to request a tool.

ToolConfiguration.description: Configuration information for the tools that you pass to a model. For more information, see Tool use (function calling) in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

ToolInputSchema.description: The schema for the tool. The top level schema type must be object. For more information, see Call a tool with the Converse API in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

json.description: The JSON schema for the tool. For more information, see JSON Schema Reference.

name.description: The name of the tool. Must match the name of a tool declared in the top-level tool configuration.

serverName.description: The name of the MCP server that provides the tool. Required when referencing an MCP tool.

ToolReference.description: A reference to a tool in the tool configuration. Used with ToolAdditionBlock and ToolRemovalBlock to identify which tool to add or remove mid-conversation.

tool.description: A reference to the tool to remove from the available tool set.

ToolRemovalBlock.description: A content block for removing a tool from the available tool set mid-conversation. Each block references a single tool via its tool field. Use within a system role message to remove a tool without re-sending the full tool configuration.

toolUseId.description: The ID of the tool request that this is the result for.

content.description: The content for tool result content block.

status.description:
The status for the tool result content block.

This field is only supported by Amazon Nova and Anthropic Claude 3 and 4 models.

type.description: The type for the tool result content block.

ToolResultBlock.description: A tool result block that contains the results for a tool request that the model previously made. For more information, see Call a tool with the Converse API in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

ToolResultBlockDelta.description: Contains incremental updates to tool results information during streaming responses. This allows clients to build up tool results data progressively as the response is generated.

json.description: The JSON schema for the tool result content block. see JSON Schema Reference.

text.description: The reasoning the model used to return the output.

toolUseId.description: The ID of the tool that was used to generate this tool result block.

type.description: The type for the tool that was used to generate this tool result block.

status.description: The status of the tool result block.

ToolResultBlockStart.description: The start of a tool result block. For more information, see Call a tool with the Converse API in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

ToolResultContentBlock.description: The tool result content block. For more information, see Call a tool with the Converse API in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

document.description: A tool result that is a document.

image.description:
A tool result that is an image.

This field is only supported by Amazon Nova and Anthropic Claude 3 and 4 models.

json.description: A tool result that is JSON format data.

searchResult.description: A tool result that is a search result.

inputSchema.description: The input schema for the tool in JSON format.

strict.description: Flag to enable structured output enforcement on a tool usage response.

ToolSpecification.description: The specification for the tool. For more information, see Call a tool with the Converse API in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

systemTool.description: Specifies the system-defined tool that you want use.

name.description: The name of the tool that the model wants to use.

input.description: The input to pass to the tool.

ToolUseBlock.description: A tool use content block. Contains information about a tool that the model is requesting be run., The model uses the result from the tool to generate a response. For more information, see Call a tool with the Converse API in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

ToolUseBlockDelta.description: The delta for a tool use block.

name.description: The name of the tool that the model is requesting to use.

ToolUseBlockStart.description: The start of a tool use block. For more information, see Call a tool with the Converse API in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.

ValidationException.description: The input fails to satisfy the constraints specified by Amazon Bedrock. For troubleshooting this error, see ValidationError in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide

VideoSource.description: A video source. You can upload a smaller video as a base64-encoded string as long as the encoded file is less than 25MB. You can also transfer videos up to 1GB in size from an S3 bucket.

s3Location.description: The location of a video object in an Amazon S3 bucket. To see which models support S3 uploads, see Supported models and features for Converse.

url.description: The URL that was cited when performing a web search.

domain.description: The domain that was cited when performing a web search.

WebLocation.description: Provides the URL and domain information for the website that was cited when performing a web search.
